title_as_printed: The PVT Properties of Concentrated Aqueous Electrolytes IX. The Volume Properties of KCl and K2SO4 and their Mixtures with NaCl and Na2SO4 as a Function of Temperature (Dedick, Hershey, Sotolongo, Stade, Millero)
experimental_method: Vibrating-tube densimeters (Sodev flow densimeter at and below 25 C, Mettler/Parr DMA 602 HT above 25 C) calibrated with water, standard seawater and nitrogen; densities of KCl and K2SO4 solutions from dilute to near saturation at 5-95 C in 10 C steps and of six binary mixtures of KCl, K2SO4, NaCl, Na2SO4 at I = 1.95 mol/kg at 5, 25, 55, 95 C.
uncertainties_stated: Bath temperatures set to +-0.002 C (HP quartz thermometer, IPTS-68), 25 C bath +-0.003 C, Mettler/Parr baths +-0.01 C; standard deviations of the density-difference fits 30 ppm (KCl) and 32 ppm (K2SO4).
quality_remarks: Some table entries look like misprints (K2SO4 Table I: 45 C m 0.16143, 0.01015; 65 C m 0.02912; 75 C m 0.56016; Table VII 55 C KCl-Na2SO4 y3 0.5028); kept as printed. Abstract says I = 2.0, table title and text say 1.95. Molality of KCl and K2SO4 solutions was derived from 25 C densities using equations of state fitted to literature and this study's data.

Table VIII: v0, v1 parameters of volume of mixing (fitted)
Table IX: temperature effect on cross square rule, maximum Delta V_m (derived)
